title: A Noetherian ring is a G-ring if its maximal localizations have geometrically regular formal fibres
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then $R$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] if and only if for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset R$ the completion map $R_{\mathfrak m}\to(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge$ is a regular ring map in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], where $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is the localization of $R$ at $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak m^nR_{\mathfrak m}$ its $\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m}$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] (in Stacks' words: $R_{\mathfrak m}$ has geometrically regular formal fibres). This is More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PT.

proof.text: ($\Rightarrow$) If $R$ is a G-ring, then for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, which is a prime ideal, the map $R_{\mathfrak m}\to(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge$ is regular by the definition of a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Definition Tag 07GH (definition-G-ring, line 12179); the direction is not written out in 07PT

proof.text: ($\Leftarrow$) Assume $R_{\mathfrak m}\to(R_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge$ is regular for every maximal $\mathfrak m$. Since $R$ is Noetherian, by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] it suffices to show that $R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ is regular for a given prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ (every proper ideal lies in a maximal ideal) and put $A=R_{\mathfrak m}$; then $\mathfrak pA$ is a prime ideal of $A$ with $\mathfrak pA\cap R=\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] to the (flat) identity map of the Noetherian ring $R$ at the primes $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak p$, $A$ and $R_{\mathfrak p}$ are Noetherian local rings. Let $c:A\to A^\wedge$ be the $\mathfrak mA$-adic completion map [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

$A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] ($\mathfrak mA$ is finitely generated as $A$ is Noetherian); so $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian complete local ring. The map $c$ is flat and $\operatorname{Spec}A^\wedge\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], so there is a prime $\mathfrak p'\subset A^\wedge$ with $c^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak pA$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), proof: 'Since R_m -> R_m^ is faithfully flat we can choose a prime p' in R_m^ lying over pR_m'

proof.text: Put $B=(A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak p'}$, with localization map $\lambda:A^\wedge\to B$, and let $c_B:B\to B^\wedge$ be the completion of $B$ at its maximal ideal $\mathfrak p'B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-g-ring] the Noetherian complete local ring $A^\wedge$ (Step 3) is a G-ring, so by the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] at its prime $\mathfrak p'$ the map $c_B$ is regular.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), proof: 'By Proposition 07PS (R_m^)_{p'} -> (R_m^)_{p'}^ is regular'

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] to the flat map $c$ between the Noetherian rings $A$ and $A^\wedge$ (Step 3) at the prime $\mathfrak p'$, $c^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak pA$: the induced map $\varphi:A_{\mathfrak pA}\to B$, $a/s\mapsto c(a)/c(s)$, is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, $\varphi(\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak pA})\subseteq\mathfrak p'B$. Here $A_{\mathfrak pA}=(R_{\mathfrak m})_{\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak m}}$ is canonically $R_{\mathfrak p}$ (both are the localization of $R$ at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$, since $R\setminus\mathfrak m\subseteq R\setminus\mathfrak p$) [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; via this identification the localization map $\ell:A\to A_{\mathfrak pA}$ is the map $R_{\mathfrak m}\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, and $\varphi\circ\ell=\lambda\circ c$ by the formula for $\varphi$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), proof: the commutative diagram

proof.text: The composite $c_B\circ\lambda\circ c:A\to B^\wedge$ is regular. Indeed $c$ is regular by hypothesis ($\mathfrak m$ maximal), $\lambda$ is regular [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular] and $c_B$ is regular (Step 4). The rings $B$ (Step 5) and $B^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] are Noetherian, so every fibre ring of a ring map into them is Noetherian: $\Lambda\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a quotient of a localization of the Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, hence Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. So [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] applied to $c$ and $\lambda$ shows $\lambda\circ c:A\to B$ regular, and applied again to $\lambda\circ c$ and $c_B$ shows $c_B\circ\lambda\circ c$ regular.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), proof: 'The localization R_m^ -> (R_m^)_{p'} is regular. Hence R_m -> (R_m^)_{p'}^ is regular by Lemma 07QI (lemma-regular-composition)'

proof.text: By Step 5, $c_B\circ\lambda\circ c=(c_B\circ\varphi)\circ\ell$ with $\ell:A\to A_{\mathfrak pA}=R_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization at the multiplicative subset $A\setminus\mathfrak pA$. Since this composite is regular (Step 6), [lem-weil-pbc-regular-through-localization] shows that $c_B\circ\varphi:R_{\mathfrak p}\to B^\wedge$ is regular.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), proof: 'Since it factors through the localization R_p, also the ring map R_p -> (R_m^)_{p'}^ is regular'

proof.text: Let $c_{\mathfrak p}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ be the completion map and $\varphi^\wedge:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ the map of completions induced by the flat local homomorphism $\varphi$ of Noetherian local rings (Step 5), so $\varphi^\wedge\circ c_{\mathfrak p}=c_B\circ\varphi$; by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-completion] $\varphi^\wedge$ is flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ and $B^\wedge$ are local with maximal ideals $\mathfrak p(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ and $\mathfrak p'B^\wedge$; as $\varphi^\wedge(c_{\mathfrak p}(x))=c_B(\varphi(x))\in\mathfrak p'B^\wedge$ for $x\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, $\varphi^\wedge$ is a local homomorphism. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}B^\wedge\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), proof: the right square of the diagram (R_p^ -> (R_m^)_{p'}^), whose flatness and surjectivity on spectra Stacks leaves implicit; flatness: More on Algebra Lemma 0C4G (lemma-flat-completion); faithful flatness: Algebra Lemma 00HR (lemma-local-flat-ff)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence] to $R_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{c_{\mathfrak p}}(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\xrightarrow{\varphi^\wedge}B^\wedge$: the composite $c_B\circ\varphi$ is regular (Step 7) and $\varphi^\wedge$ is flat and surjective on spectra (Step 8), so $c_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular. As $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary and $R$ is Noetherian, $R$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

Proof follows Stacks in 9 steps: the trivial direction; choice of m containing p and a prime p' of (R_m)^ over pR_m (00MC); 07PS at p' for the Noetherian complete local ring (R_m)^; the identification (R_m)_{pR_m}=R_p and the flat local map phi: R_p -> (R_m^)_{p'}; two applications of 07QI (fibre rings Noetherian since the targets are Noetherian) with the regularity of a localization; descent of regularity through the localization R_m -> R_p; flatness (0C4G) and Spec surjectivity (00HR) of phi^: R_p^ -> (R_m^)_{p'}^, which Stacks leaves implicit; 07NT. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-g-ring (07PS), lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition (07QI), lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular and lem-weil-pbc-regular-through-localization (asserted without proof in 07PT), lem-weil-pbc-flat-completion (0C4G, one direction), all unsplit; lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat (00HR), Mathlib leaf Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom with PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat. Existing nodes reused: 07NT, 00MC (also gives the flatness of c, so 00MB is not cited), adic-completion-noetherian, local-completion-local-ring, adic-completion-mod-ideal, flat-local-ring-maps. 07C0 (lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal) is not needed by this proof.
